classification.difficultyReason: Identify success probabilities in each context, interpret repeated names as replacement, and group ordered two- or three-trial paths by the same count before tabulating probabilities. These are routine linked applications of the taught tree method.

content.prompt:
These questions require you to find the probabilities using a tree diagram, or otherwise.
Construct a probability distribution table for the given discrete random variable.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
A pack of cards has 52 cards, of which 12 are court cards.
Two cards are drawn with replacement, and it is recorded whether or not each is a court card.
Let $X$ be the number of court cards drawn.

inlines.text: Let C mean court card and
mean not a court card. Replacement keeps the probabilities unchanged.

spec.description: Two-draw binary tree with complement bars, outcome and probability columns; no branch probabilities printed.
spec.mathematics: Court probability 3/13 on each draw; four ordered outcomes have probabilities 9/169, 30/169, 30/169 and 100/169.

children.label: b
children.prompt:
Three dice are thrown, and the number of even numbers is recorded.
Let $X$ be the number of even numbers when the three dice are thrown.

. The eight ordered parity outcomes are equally likely. There are respectively 1, 3, 3 and 1 outcomes with 0, 1, 2 and 3 even results.
